analysis.title: Global Reflections (Nick Savone, IED sales commentary), 10 Oct 2026
key_insights: Index and market breadth diverge. The S&P 500 is near record highs (0.2% from an all-time high) and MSCI World is up 13.5% YTD. The Russell 2000 has fallen five straight weeks and 54% of Russell 3000 stocks have drawn down more than 20% since June, while earnings growth stays healthy.

The note frames 3Q earnings season as the test for the bull/bear debate. Rates, oil and AI capex and financing are the main worries. Tuesday's bank earnings and Wednesday's US CPI are the first reads.

Early reports are mixed. PepsiCo beat a low bar but cut guidance, which raises a question about a 2027 EPS reset. Levi Strauss raised its FY outlook despite softer revenue. Constellation Brands beat but weak beer demand and margin pressure remain. Delta's September-quarter revenue rose about 16% YoY.

Global P/E multiples contracted 8% in 3Q, the largest de-rating in a rising market since 1994, despite constructive earnings revisions. More stable yields could ease valuation pressure without a Treasury rally.

Consensus expects 29.5% YoY S&P 500 3Q EPS growth in this note, with the Mag7 contributing roughly a quarter. Mike Wilson cites 27% EPS growth and 10% sales growth, with the median stock growing EPS 14%. September core CPI is forecast at 0.24% MoM versus 0.29% in August.

Asia: the AI trade had a less comfortable week as higher oil and yields prompted profit-taking in crowded growth names, mostly in Korea and Japan. Hong Kong rebounded late. Samsung reported strong preliminary earnings and TSMC September revenue grew nearly 55% YoY. Interest is broadening from memory to substrates, MLCCs and semiconductor chemicals.

Europe: French political risk is moving from bonds into equities, with sovereign spreads near 140bps. EUR/USD fell to 1.12, a 17-month low, and the STOXX 600 hit a four-month low led by banks. Tesco's profit beat is cited as evidence of corporate resilience. The UK Budget is a fiscal test for Sterling.

US bank positioning: Manan Gosalia expects a neutral 3Q for large cap banks, with 14%/13% median EPS growth in 2027/2028 and banks at about 10x/9x forward earnings. Preferred names are STT, C, BAC and FITB. US banks are down 13% since August with a 14D RSI of 27 versus above 60 for the S&P 500, the widest RSI gap since 1993.

The MS Cross-Asset Market Sentiment Indicator turned positive, exiting the risk-off signal held since 21 July 2026. This regime has been associated with above-average one-week forward global equity returns.

Credit: US HY spreads are at the 16th percentile since 1994, but CCC spreads are above 1,000bps, the widest since 2023, and the ratio of CCC to HY spreads is at a record high. Similar CCC levels in 1998, 2011, 2015 and 2022 did not immediately signal recession, but this divergence has tended to peak before a worse credit cycle.

Dispersion: S&P 500 dispersion is in the 79th percentile versus 5Y, single-name vol in the 40th percentile, and the sector-versus-within-sector dispersion ratio in the 28th percentile. This points to stock-specific rather than sector or macro-driven dispersion, which earnings season may amplify.

Gold is the Derivatives Sales top commodity pick, with the pullback seen as an entry point. The thesis is that it can work with higher or lower rates. Central banks bought 289t in 2Q26 and ETF holdings keep rising despite Fed hikes. Gold trades above its historical relationship with real yields.

Prime brokerage: funds were larger net sellers of global equities, with US selling the largest since July, driven by long reductions in TMT (semis, optical networking, agentic AI beneficiaries) and Health Care. Funds favored Defensives over Cyclicals. US L/S net leverage is flat at 52% and gross rose to 207%. Americas L/S is down 0.4% MTD versus S&P +1.5%.

Gapen sees policy as neutral to modestly restrictive. His real neutral rate estimate rose from under 100bps to about 150bps since early 2025, and financial conditions have tightened 100bps since February. He forecasts two further 25bps Fed hikes in December and March, to 4.25-4.50%, and September core CPI at 0.24% MoM and headline at 0.62% MoM.

Cross-asset: Serena Tang notes US Treasury yields at 5.30%, the highest since 2002, a 2.2% Hang Seng drop and Brent briefly below $100/bbl as Middle East flows recovered. US ETFs took in $13.8B of equities and $12.8B of government bonds. Her framework favors defensive diversifiers such as Staples and Utilities.

France: Jens Eisenschmidt says France needs a primary surplus of 2% of GDP to stabilize debt, a EUR150B adjustment, and sees public debt near 160% of GDP by 2040. The ECB could pause QT if yields keep rising, and a France-Germany 10Y spread above 200bps is a possible TPI threshold.

Marina Zavolock stays constructive on European equities, noting that nearly two-thirds of EUR IG bonds mature after 2030 and about 5% EBITDA growth offsets today's yields. She names oversold Overweight stocks (GLE FP, UCG IM, HEI GR, NG/ LN). She sees only 3% of MSCI Europe at moderate or higher agentic AI disruption risk.

Japan: crude imports averaged 2.35M b/d in August at about USD103/bbl, with a premium over Dubai futures above USD25/bbl. Takeshi Yamaguchi sees a wider trade deficit weakening the yen, Japan core CPI temporarily above 3% YoY as energy subsidies expire, and BoJ hikes in December and March.

AI and hyperscalers: Stephen Byrd estimates a 34% net US power shortfall through 2028. MS argues hyperscalers (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, SPCX) are best placed for the next AI phase, with Microsoft singled out for monetization across Azure, Fabric, Foundry and Copilot. AlphaWise finds net AI sentiment of +14% but -20% for data centers within about 10 miles, with opposition up to 41% from 25%.

Alphabet: Brian Nowak sees Waymo as an underappreciated physical AI differentiator and raises 2027/2028 trip forecasts by 4%/3%, with about 1.1B annual trips and about $21B revenue by 2032. GOOGL is Overweight with a $400 PT at about 19x 2028 EPS.

Mike Wilson favors quality and calls Industrials the best risk/reward, with Capital Goods revisions breadth at 38%. His Industrials screen includes CAT, GD, ITW and EME, and his Fresh Money Buy List includes TGT, NOC and AMT.

Rating changes in the MS single-name section: WFC upgraded to OW ($102, top pick), BWA to OW ($95 from $71), CBOE double-upgraded to OW from UW, Continental to OW (EUR78), NEXA to OW ($14.20), SHEIN initiated at OW (HKD58), and GPI downgraded to UW. Informa OW reiterated.

Negative research: Erik Woodring forecasts PC shipments down 14% Y/Y in CY26 and 11% in CY27, 7 points below consensus, with HPQ ($19 PT, 41% downside) and Acer (25% downside) as high-conviction UWs. Marina Massuti stays cautious on traditional European asset managers given valuations and higher rates.

SpaceX is buying 14 MHz of low-band spectrum from Grain Management, adding to about 65 MHz from EchoStar. MS sees Starlink Mobile at about 9M subscribers by 2032, a competitive risk for T, TMUS and VZ and possibly a benefit for AMT.

MS European Derivatives highlights MSSTWKBS (weak balance sheet basket) downside protection as a hedge against rising yields, CDS spreads, French stress and Brent near $105. The basket fell 20% in the 2022 rising-rate episode and implied vol is currently below SX5E.

Bank M&A: Ryan Kenny expects acceleration as regulatory hurdles ease and smaller banks face technology costs. The MS Banks M&A basket (MSXXBKMA) includes SSB, OZK and FNB, with a webcast on Monday Oct 12 at 12pm ET.

Agentic commerce (Albert Lin): favors WMT, COST and W for scale and fulfillment. RCL and CCL could gain from lower distribution costs. PLNT and CHWY face subscription cancellation and price competition risks.

earnings_insights: 3Q S&P 500 EPS growth: consensus 29.5% YoY per Savone's closing paragraph (estimate, not yet reported), with Mag7 expected to contribute roughly a quarter. Mike Wilson cites consensus of 27% EPS growth and 10% sales growth for 3Q (estimate). The chart title cites +27% Y/Y.
PepsiCo (PEP) reported a beat against a relatively low bar, but a guidance cut raised questions about a potential 2027 EPS reset.
Levi Strauss (LEVI) reported improving US DTC trends and a higher FY outlook despite softer revenues.
Constellation Brands (STZ) reported a beat, with weaker beer demand and margin pressure still in focus.
Delta Air Lines (DAL) reported September-quarter revenue up about 16% YoY with momentum continuing into year-end.
Tesco (TSCO LN) delivered a solid profit beat despite disinflation and tougher comparisons.
Samsung Electronics (005930 KS) issued strong preliminary earnings. TSMC (2330 TT) reported September revenue growth of nearly 55% YoY, with full results approaching.

Large cap banks: Tuesday's bank earnings start the season. Gosalia expects a relatively neutral 3Q with capital markets activity moderating ahead of the midterms, and forecasts median EPS growth of 14% in 2027 and 13% in 2028 (estimates).
Single-name implied volatility is elevated, particularly in Industrials and Financials, so the market may reward delivery and punish misses.
Wilson expects earnings quality, free cash flow and revisions breadth to drive differentiation in 3Q, as in 2Q.
Waymo 1H26 miles came in about 3% below expectations, per Brian Nowak.
Mike Cyprys sees CBOE options growth as more durable than he expected, with KPI prediction markets adding upside not yet in estimates.

Credit: CCC spreads above 1,000bps and a record CCC-to-HY spread ratio point to stress among the weakest borrowers and refinancing risk.
French sovereign and fiscal stress, with a France-Germany 10Y spread above 200bps cited as a possible ECB TPI threshold.

Weaker yen and wider trade deficit in Japan from energy import costs.
Capital markets activity moderating ahead of the US midterms, and 3Q M&A cooling from record 2Q levels.

Financials single-name vol is relatively subdued, in the 15th 5Y percentile.
US Equity L/S net leverage is flat at 52% (52nd percentile versus 2010) and gross rose 1% WoW to 207% (91st percentile).
Funds were net sellers across all regions outside the US, led by Japan and China, with a notable rotation away from high-conviction longs in Europe.
Americas L/S is down 0.4% MTD versus +1.5% for the S&P, Europe and Asia L/S are down 0.7%. YTD the average global fund is up 7.0%.

European banks: SX7E net exposure fell to the 25th percentile and option markets are negative.

French political and fiscal risk is spreading from sovereign bonds into equities, with spreads near 140bps.
UK fiscal test ahead of the October Budget, with a slower consolidation path keeping Sterling in focus.

US midterm elections are cited as moderating capital markets activity.
